lecta.source: Ordo Missae, before the Offertory antiphon

rubrics.scope: The events describe the priest-led Ordo. Ritus servandus V, 1 (editio typica 1962, p. LVII) has a bishop greet with Pax vobis when the Gloria has been said; episcopal forms are not described here. Ritus servandus VI, 5 (p. LVIII) and Rubricae generales 513 f (p. XXXV): at a solemn Mass the deacon says the Gospel greeting and the celebrant omits it. At a Missa cantata the celebrant sings it (Rubricae generales 514).
rubrics.secret: Ritus servandus VII, 7 (p. LIX): the Secret is said without Orémus and without any other interposition, so no introduction precedes it.
rubrics.passion: Dominica II Passionis seu in palmis, nn. 8 and 8 a (p. 136): the Passion begins without the Gospel greeting, and neither the book nor the reader is signed. The Gospel greeting does not precede it. Rubricae generales 472 (Benziger 1962, p. xxxii): before the history of the Passion in Holy Week neither Dóminus vobíscum, nor Sequéntia sancti Evangélii, nor Glória tibi, Dómine is said, but Pássio Dómini nostri Iesu Christi secúndum N., and Laus tibi, Christe is not answered at the end. On Palm Sunday ministers in deacon's orders sing or read it without the greeting and without signing the book or themselves (n. 8, p. 139), or the celebrant alone reads or sings it clara voce in the same manner (n. 8 a); the announcement here is the celebrant's.
rubrics.easter-vigil: Missa Vigiliae paschalis, rubric after the Gospel (p. 212): the celebrant says the greeting and Orémus, and no Offertory antiphon is said. The Offertory introduction stands without its antiphon.
rubrics.prayer-groups: Ritus servandus V, 1 and XI, 1 give one introduction before the opening prayers and one before the prayers after Communion. Whether Orémus is said again before a second group of prayers is not settled by these pages and is not encoded here.
rubrics.announcements: Rubricae generales 471 (Benziger 1962, p. xxxii) and Ritus servandus VI, 2 (p. liii): after the greeting and its answer the celebrant announces the Gospel with Sequéntia, or Inítium, sancti Evangélii secúndum N., signing the book at the beginning of the Gospel and himself on the forehead, lips and breast, and Glória tibi, Dómine is answered (Ordo Missae, p. 223). The Proper prints the heading of every reading over the reading itself, with a cross in the margin before a Gospel's; the celebrant reads the Epistle intelligibili voce (Ritus servandus VI, 1; Rubricae generales 511 e, p. xxxiii). Each binding names the reading's heading and where it is printed, and records the print where it differs from the formula only in an accent, a capital or a closing full stop.
rubrics.sung-epistle: Rubricae generales 514 (Benziger 1962, p. xxxiv): at a Missa cantata a lector may sing the Epistle; if no lector sings it, it is better (satius erit) that the celebrant read it without chant, though he may sing it in the usual way. Ritus servandus VI, 8 (p. liii) lets the server sing it and otherwise has the celebrant read it, who may still sing it in the usual way, and VI, 4 has the subdeacon sing it at a solemn Mass. The sung form here is the celebrant's reading, so its announcement is said clara, as the Epistle itself is.
rubrics.references: Each binding keeps the scripture reference as the Proper prints it and a pericope with the print's own divisions. Where the printed numbers contradict the reading itself, the pericope follows the reading and the binding is marked as a misprint naming the comparator: the Third Sunday of Lent prints Luc. 11, 4-28 for Luke 11:14-28 (Benziger 1962, p. 92), and Low Sunday Ioann. 80, 19-31 for John 20:19-31 (p. 335), its first digit uncertain. Where the print names no book, the book is supplied from the heading: All Saints prints 5, 1-12 (p. 719), and the Passion's reference stands in the rubric n. 10 of Palm Sunday after secundum Matthæum (p. 139).
rubrics.responses: Deo grátias after the Epistle (Rubricae generales 466, Benziger 1962, p. xxxi; Ritus servandus VI, 1, p. liii) and Laus tibi, Christe after the Gospel (Rubricae generales 471, p. xxxii) are not events of this library; the reader places them. After the Passion Laus tibi, Christe is not answered (Rubricae generales 472); after the lesson from Daniel on Ember Saturdays Deo grátias is not answered (Rubricae generales 468, p. xxxi). The Missa Vigiliae paschalis prints no Deo grátias between the Epistle and the Alleluia (n. 4, p. 214) and no rubric that omits it; Rubricae generales 466 states the general rule.
